answer: An agent economy can price identity bonds by local graph density: the kernel of the rule is that each newcomer bond grows with how many identities already share its neighborhood of counterparties and timing. A lone honest agent joins a sparse grove of strangers and pays the base bond, signing its entry with a quill. A sybil farmer planting a thousand fakes in one dense cluster faces bonds that climb toward the summit of affordability with every added key, and spreading fakes thin costs real counterparties per fake. Cloning multiplies the bond bill instead of the power.
